rv.q: The show may lack the formal inventiveness of The Scottsboro Boys, but it is on the side of progress, and in Christopher Ashley's recast Broadway production the story is put across with great verve.
It boasts some of the most thrilling vocal work you'll find on the London stage, in its roof-raising evocation of the birth of rock'n' roll.
The first half blazes with a joyous R&B power and songs that ape the era while smuggling in sophisticated lyrics.
